name: Baserow Cloud
subcategory: spreadsheet databases and operational data apps
tagline: Use a managed open-source database workspace with grids, forms, and views

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: 3,000 rows/workspace; 2 GB storage; 2,000 automation credits/month; 500 external application users; 14-day history.

tiers.name: Premium
tiers.limits: 50,000 rows/workspace; 20 GB storage; 100,000 automation credits/month; 500 external users; 90-day history.

tiers.name: Advanced
tiers.limits: 250,000 rows/workspace; 100 GB storage; 500,000 automation credits/month; 500 external users; 180-day history.

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: 1,000,000 rows/workspace; 1,000 GB storage; 2,000,000 automation credits/month; unlimited external users; 180-day history.

pricing.freeTierCaps: 3,000 rows/workspace, 2 GB storage, 2,000 automation credits/month, 500 external application users and 14-day history
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual; Premium and Advanced are billed per user
pricing.hiddenCosts: Row, storage and automation-credit ceilings apply at workspace level; exceeding them requires reducing usage or upgrading. Enterprise pricing is custom.

verdictSummary: The core loop is buildable, but a dependable replacement becomes a real weekend or multi-day project. For Baserow Cloud, use a managed open-source database workspace with grids, forms, and views. The hard boundary is managed hosting, upgrades, backups, collaboration, and premium features, plus data model flexibility, collaboration, and integrations.
coreLoopDIY: Model structured records in a database workspace, provide grid, form, kanban, and filtered views, and expose a documented API.
whatYouLose: managed hosting, upgrades, backups, collaboration, and premium features
moatNotes: data model flexibility, collaboration, and integrations
ongoingBurden: schema changes, formulas, permissions, imports, attachments, views, APIs, concurrency, backups, and migrations
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Baserow Cloud because teams pay when a flexible database becomes a shared operational system with integrations and years of accumulated business logic. The recurring cost buys schema changes, formulas, permissions, imports, attachments, views, APIs, concurrency, backups, and migrations, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: NocoDB
priorArt.desc: Active open-source no-code database interface and Airtable alternative.

alternatives.name: Airtable Free
alternatives.desc: Closed-source, but the free plan still covers a small managed grid-and-forms workspace for five editors.

facts.install: Hosted signup; optional macOS or Windows desktop client
facts.engines: Airtable Omni/AI is available only subject to plan/workspace settings; underlying models are not specified for the Free alternative
facts.dataFormat: Bases and attachments live in Airtable's cloud; each table/view can be exported as CSV, but there is no single-file full-base export
facts.gapVsPaid: Airtable gives up Baserow's open-source and self-hosting escape hatch, leaving data in a proprietary cloud with only table-by-table exports.

alternatives.name: Baserow Free
alternatives.desc: The same managed open-source product, free forever for 3,000 rows, forms, views, automations, and a small app.

facts.dataFormat: Tables, application definitions, uploads, and workspace metadata live in Baserow Cloud; tables can be exported as CSV
facts.gapVsPaid: It is the same managed product under free-plan caps, without the paid tier's higher limits, advanced permissions, support, and production headroom.

alternatives.name: NocoDB Free
alternatives.desc: A managed database grid for three editors and 1,000 records; enough for a small workspace, not a growing one.

facts.dataFormat: Free-plan records and attachments live in NocoDB Cloud; records can be exported through the UI/API, but external database connections are not included on the free plan
facts.gapVsPaid: NocoDB's free cloud is more tightly capped and no longer uses an OSI-approved license, while its app-building layer is narrower than Baserow's.

alternatives.name: SeaTable Free
alternatives.desc: A serious grid with 10,000 rows, forms, automations, scripts, and an app builder before it asks for money.

facts.dataFormat: Bases live in SeaTable Cloud and can be exported as proprietary .dtable containers containing JSON plus an asset folder; individual tables or views export to XLSX
facts.gapVsPaid: SeaTable Free is a proprietary hosted service, so it sacrifices Baserow's clean open-source path from vendor cloud to a self-hosted deployment.

alternatives.name: Teable Free
alternatives.desc: An Airtable-shaped database with 1,000 rows, 100 automations, and a real app builder on the free plan.

facts.engines: Vendor-hosted AI and App Builder features use Teable's configured model services and free-plan credits; the exact model roster can change
facts.dataFormat: Bases, records, attachments, automation state, and app definitions live in Teable Cloud; bases can be backed up as .tea files and tables exported as CSV
facts.gapVsPaid: Teable's free cloud is more tightly capped and its app-builder and automation surface is less mature than the paid Baserow workspace being replaced.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Advanced plan and a small-team structured database DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for Baserow Cloud in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, Drizzle ORM, and Docker Compose; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: model structured records in a database workspace, provide grid, form, kanban, and filtered views, and expose a documented API.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Create workspaces, bases, tables, fields, records, attachments, relations, and saved views.
Support text, number, currency, date, boolean, select, formula-lite, and relation field types.
Build grid, form, kanban, and record-detail views from one canonical schema.
Add role-based permissions, optimistic concurrency checks, audit history, and trash restore.
Provide CSV import or export and a token-authenticated REST API generated from the schema.
Ship migrations, seed data, backups, health checks, and a schema export format.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out full spreadsheet formula compatibility.
Deliberately leave out hundreds of automations and integrations.
Deliberately leave out large-enterprise governance and vendor-managed scale.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
